1. `./b4w.ps1 -s research goto "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Browser_automation"`
2. `./b4w.ps1 -s news goto "https://news.ycombinator.com"`

6. `./b4w.ps1 -s news close`
7. `./b4w.ps1 list`
8. `./b4w.ps1 close-all`

- Used `snapshot -v 0 --stdout` to view content inline rather than opening YAML files, following the SKILL.md template
- Used `close` with `-s` flag to target a specific session — the pattern works but is not explicitly documented
- Used `close-all` for bulk cleanup

- None strictly required. All commands worked as expected on first attempt.
- The `-v` flag produced a warning about PowerShell compatibility on every snapshot call, despite the SKILL.md claiming `b4w.ps1` handles short flags safely. This is a noise issue, not a functional blocker.

issues.title: snapshot --stdout output is overwhelming for first-time users

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: $(./b4w.ps1) -s news snapshot -v 0 --stdout

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: A concise, scannable view of the page structure suitable for quick verification. The SKILL.md recommends --stdout for "quick inline viewing."

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Hacker News produced 64KB of YAML output. Wikipedia produced 37KB. The output is too large to read in a terminal and was truncated by the tool harness. First-time users following the copy-paste template in SKILL.md would be overwhelmed.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: Even with -v 0 (single viewport), the AX tree for content-rich pages contains hundreds of lines. The SKILL.md template encourages --stdout without adequately warning about output volume. The snapshot output includes detailed box coordinates for every element, which adds significant volume.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add a --summary or --brief mode to snapshot that prints only page title, URL, and top-level structure (headings, link count, form elements) without full AX tree
- Update the SKILL.md copy-paste template to warn about expected output size and suggest snapshot grep for targeted verification
- Consider limiting --stdout output to a configurable line count with a "...truncated" message, similar to how get html already paginates at 2K lines

issues.title: No documented way to close a single named session

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Search the help output and SKILL.md for instructions on closing a single named session.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Documentation showing how to close a specific session, e.g., a 'close' command with -s flag, or a dedicated subcommand like 'session-close <name>'.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The help output lists 'close' as "Close the browser" with no mention of session targeting. SKILL.md's session section (§2) describes opening and listing but not closing individual sessions. The -s <name> close pattern works but is discoverable only by trial and error.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The close command supports -s targeting but neither the help text nor the SKILL.md document this. The help text "Close the browser" implies closing everything, not a single session. The session management section in SKILL.md (§2) covers open, list, and session-default but omits close.

sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Update help text: 'close — Close the current browser session (use -s <name> to close a specific named session)'
- Add a dedicated 'Closing sessions' subsection to SKILL.md §2 showing: browser4-cli -s <name> close, browser4-cli close (closes default), browser4-cli close-all
- Consider adding a 'session-close <name>' alias for explicit session closing

issues.title: b4w.ps1 emits short-flag warnings for -v despite SKILL.md claiming safety

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: $(./b4w.ps1) -s news snapshot -v 0 --stdout

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: No warning — SKILL.md states b4w.ps1 "Uses manual $args parsing so common short flags (-o/-i/-v) are no longer intercepted by PowerShell's parameter binder."

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Every invocation emits: "⚠ Short flags detected: -v. PowerShell may intercept these in other contexts (b4w.sh, direct pwsh). Prefer long-form equivalents: --output, --interactive, --viewport. Or use b4w.sh / b4w.bat (cmd.exe) for full compatibility."

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The CLI's argument parser unconditionally emits a warning when short flags like -v are detected, even when invoked through b4w.ps1 which handles them safely. The warning logic does not check whether the invocation context is already safe. This creates a contradiction with the SKILL.md documentation.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/ (argument parsing or warning emission logic)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Suppress the short-flag warning when the CLI detects it is running through b4w.ps1 (e.g., via an env var or argv[0] check)
- Or remove the warning entirely for short flags that b4w.ps1 now handles safely, and only warn for truly problematic contexts (b4w.sh, direct pwsh)
- Alternatively, provide a --no-warn-short-flags option to suppress these warnings

issues.title: Auto-created default session appears in list despite user never creating it

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run $(./b4w.ps1) list after creating only named sessions with -s <name> goto.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Only the two named sessions (research, news) appear, or the default session is hidden/minimized unless explicitly targeted.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Three sessions appear: 'news', 'research', and '(default)'. The default session was auto-created by a prior (possibly unrelated) goto/open call. The footnote about '(default)' being "safe to close or switch away from" helps but is easily missed.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The unnamed default session persists from prior commands or is auto-created on first use. session-default <name> can reassign it but doesn't remove it. New users may not understand where this session came from or whether they need to manage it.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Consider not auto-creating a default session until the user explicitly invokes goto or open without -s
- Add a '--named-only' flag to list that filters out the default session
- Highlight the default session footnote more prominently (or show it only when a default session actually exists)

issues.title: close command says 'Browser terminated' when only one session is closed

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: $(./b4w.ps1) -s news close

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Session closed. Or: Session 'news' closed.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Session closed. Browser terminated.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The close command's output message is generic and assumes closing the browser entirely rather than a single session. When -s targets a named session, the message still says "Browser terminated" which is misleading — other sessions (e.g., 'research') remain active.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/ (close command output formatting)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- When -s <name> is used, output: "Session '<name>' closed." instead of "Browser terminated."
- When closing the default session without -s, output: "Default session closed. Browser terminated."
- Reserve "Browser terminated" only for cases where the last remaining session was closed

issues.title: Snapshot output mixes AX tree with viewport metadata in a confusing format

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: $(./b4w.ps1) -s news snapshot -v 0 --stdout

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Clear separation between metadata (viewport info, page URL/title) and AX tree content.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The output begins with YAML comments (# Viewport State, # - processingViewport, etc.) then dives directly into the AX tree. Page URL and title are shown separately in the command output (outside --stdout). The metadata-comment format (lines starting with #) is unusual for a YAML tool and may confuse users expecting structured data.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: Snapshot output uses YAML comments for viewport metadata and regular YAML for the AX tree. This hybrid format is not standard YAML and cannot be parsed by YAML tools without preprocessing. The page-level information (URL, title) appears in the command's human-readable output, not in the --stdout stream, fragmenting the information.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/snapshot.rs

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Move viewport metadata into the YAML structure as top-level keys instead of comments, so the entire output is valid, parseable YAML
- Include page URL and title in the --stdout output so users get a self-contained snapshot
- Consider a --meta-only flag that prints just the metadata without the AX tree
